name: Eriksen Estring
question: Does an estradiol-releasing vaginal ring delay recurrent urinary tract infection in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Women at least 2 years after menopause with at least 3 treated UTIs in the preceding year; the most recent infection was bacteriologically confirmed.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, p 1073; Results, p 1075

verdictNote: Time to first recurrence favored the ring (log-rank P = 0.008).
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with recurrent urinary tract infection, the estradiol-releasing vaginal ring Estring prolonged time to first recurrence versus no estrogen treatment; estimated infection-free survival at 36 weeks was approximately 45% versus 20% (log-rank P = 0.008).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Eriksen BC. "A randomized, open, parallel-group study on the preventive effect of an estradiol-releasing vaginal ring (Estring) on recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 1999;180(5):1072-1079. doi:10.1016/S0002-9378(99)70597-1
reports.followUp: 36 weeks of ring treatment; controls followed for 36 weeks or until first recurrence

results.measure: Kaplan–Meier estimate of remaining free of UTI at 36 weeks
results.note: ITT and per-protocol Kaplan–Meier curves are shown; 9 ring recipients and 5 controls were excluded from the primary per-protocol analysis. The reported log-rank P value is 0.008. These estimates are not crude event proportions; no HR, confidence interval, or prespecified alpha is reported.
results.locator: Full text, Fig 1 and Results, p 1075

results.measure: Women with a symptomatic, bacteriologically confirmed recurrence during observation (ITT)
results.note: Controls left observation at first recurrence; these crude counts are distinct from the Kaplan–Meier estimates.

results.measure: Vaginal pH decrease and vaginal and urethral cell maturation

values.exp: Lower vaginal pH; more mature vaginal and, to a lesser extent, urethral mucosal cells

results.note: Vaginal and urethral maturation-value changes differed between groups (both P < .001); ring-group pH fell from baseline to week 12 (P < .001). No numeric arm-specific maturation or pH values are printed.
results.locator: Full text, Laboratory efficacy variables and Fig 2, p 1076

results.measure: Free of vaginal mucosal atrophy at termination (ITT; among women with baseline atrophy)
results.note: Denominators are the baseline atrophy counts; no interval or prespecified threshold is reported.

results.measure: Symptom-free change among participants symptomatic at baseline (ITT)
results.note: Urge P = .03; stress P = .003; symptom-specific denominators are not printed.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Events of vaginal bleeding and nonphysiologic discharge, p 1077
harms.note: The investigators judged a causal relationship with ring treatment unlikely. New or worsened event counts were higher with the ring (P = .039), but the proportion of subjects with a new adverse event did not differ (P = 1.0).

harms.label: Vaginal bleeding and nonphysiologic discharge after treatment start
harms.locator: Full text, Events of vaginal bleeding and nonphysiologic discharge, p 1077
harms.note: Events were specifically solicited at visits; no Clavien–Dindo grades, mesh exposure, or reoperation data are reported.

harms.label: Withdrawal before completion or first recurrence
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 1075; Adverse events, p 1077
harms.note: The authors considered the two ring-group own-wish withdrawals plausibly adverse-event related; no control subject withdrew because of an adverse event.

delivery.label: Ring regimen
delivery.value: The 2 mg 17β-estradiol silicone ring was placed in the upper third of the vaginal vault, worn continuously for 12 ± 2 weeks, replaced at weeks 12 and 24, and removed at week 36.

relations.note: Both found fewer recurrences with vaginal estrogen; Eriksen tested an estradiol ring against no estrogen treatment.
